Gaps carried over from the previous round (keep their ids):
\- gap-1 [ACADEMIC, HIGH]: The corpus still does not establish a complete method for maintaining evidence provenance across successive workplace attachment revisions, including stable attachment identity, version-relative source locations, semantic changes between versions, and lineage from an older cited region to its later counterpart. VersionRAG covers explicit version-aware retrieval in technical documentation, and 2607.14117 covers cross-version element alignment in scientific PDFs, but neither validates the complete attachment-revision provenance problem.
    suggested query: "document version alignment" multimodal provenance region lineage semantic change revised documents
    searched in rounds: [1, 2] (still open)
\- gap-2 [ACADEMIC, HIGH]: Direct grounding of workplace-message language such as "this screenshot", "the highlighted row", or "numbers below" into an attachment, cell, page element, or document region remains unvalidated. Scene-text referring-expression comprehension and visually grounded dialogue provide adjacent-domain mechanisms but not email-to-attachment evaluation.
    suggested query: "referring expression grounding" document multimodal email attachment table cell screenshot coreference
    searched in rounds: [1, 2] (still open)
\- gap-3 [ACADEMIC, HIGH]: Spreadsheet understanding beyond isolated tables remains open. The newer spreadsheet papers cover workbook-level inspection, structure extraction, verification, multi-sheet business workflows, and target-cell modification, but the corpus still does not establish comprehensive treatment of formulas, hidden rows or sheets, cross-sheet references, merged regions, formatting semantics, units, named ranges, and provenance across revised workbook versions.
    suggested query: "spreadsheet understanding" workbook formulas hidden sheets named ranges merged cells cross-sheet provenance
    searched in rounds: [1, 2] (still open)
\- gap-4 [ACADEMIC, HIGH]: No admitted paper validates an end-to-end provenance representation that jointly identifies attachment version, page, document element, exact region or cell, and answer span. Individual studies validate different subsets of this hierarchy, but their combination remains untested.
    suggested query: "evidence provenance" document question answering page region cell answer span multimodal grounding
    searched in rounds: [1, 2] (still open)
\- gap-5 [ENGINEERING, HIGH]: End-to-end behavior when extraction or grounding is unsupported, incomplete, or wrong remains insufficiently exercised. The corpus contains unanswerable-question evaluation and analyses of parser, localization, retrieval, OCR, and grounding failures, but no complete engineering contract distinguishing successful absence from parser, OCR, layout, or grounding failure.
\- gap-6 [ENGINEERING, HIGH]: Robustness of candidate extraction and structural-preservation pipelines on heterogeneous workplace documents remains an engineering gap. Existing studies expose failures involving sparse tables, heterogeneous reading order, OCR dependence, parser coverage, and layout errors, but do not jointly benchmark sparse tables, merged structures, OCR corruption, irregular reading order, embedded images, and scanned pages under one workplace-style test suite.
\- gap-7 [ENGINEERING, MEDIUM]: Operational scaling remains open for long documents, large tables, and spreadsheet workbooks. Reported methods expose quadratic table-relation inference, page-count memory pressure, information loss under page compression, model input cut-offs or merging, and substantial multi-agent extraction latency.
\- gap-8 [ENGINEERING, HIGH]: The corpus lacks one evaluation that simultaneously scores semantic correctness, extraction completeness, exact provenance, unsupported-evidence handling, and preservation of tables, images, and reading order on workplace-style attachments. Existing benchmarks and metrics cover subsets of these properties rather than the complete combination.
